questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The location and the country and that the location had a divers set of courses that was in the filed of my studie.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
That was a bit harder. Especially with info on accommodations and how you can use your free time on campus or even in clubs.   

For a UCPH student we were missing info on how you choose courses and if we could get them.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: How to get courses,

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Glendon or Keele

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Needed to pay 2000 CAD and did not have any cooking facilities which i found weird. At first the food was fine but at the end if became to much of the same. Also the prices where almost a extortion of students.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: You meet people the university, but the food can be expensive and same old, same old.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: People need to be made aware of the proces before the arrive.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Some mails with representative and online catelog, but no induction into what courses that you can have depending on potential schedule conflict before arrival only after. so if there was a conflict you had to choose other courses then the ones that you had in mind when coming originally.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer:
Got contacted 2 week maybe less, to get my courses via mail and had some zoom meetings 

2 weeks is to late

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
Not really since I didn't have the schedule builder:
https://registrar.yorku.ca/enrol/guide/vsb
Use it, it's worth it :D

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: contact the faculty you what to take courses from and get them to help you or even the team in charge of exchange students.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
I had 3'rd and 4'th year courses

Some courses where add-on's from what i had learned before and others were new for me.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Participation and course assignments counted much more in the final grade than what it would have done at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- EU/GEOG4440 N - Processing and Analysis of Earth Observation (Winter 2021-2022) (Lab 01)
- EU/ENVS3226 M - Sustainable Urbanism: Environmental Planning and Design (Winter 2021-2022)
- EU/GEOG3230 N - Environmental Politics in Latin America and the Caribbean (Winter 2021-2022)
- EU/GEOG3800 M - Geographies of Work (Winter 2021-2022)
- EU/GEOG4440 N - Processing and Analysis of Earth Observation (Winter 2021-2022)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Environmental Politics in Latin America and the Caribbean
The course structure was great :) It was a course that wasn't in my original study.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The transportation was a bit more expensive than expected, the food at campus was more expensive as well.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I arrived at the beginning of January, but the non-academic opportunities opened up in February due to covid19.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a big fitness center on campus. There are big social areas on campus, but they were unfortunately closed due to covid19. There are many clubs, but it is expected that you take initiative to join the clubs yourself if interest arises. If you live on campus, the local don team (consisting of students who help you while living on campus) will arrange social events.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: University parties are great!! :D And if you can find activities going off-campus and seeing the surroundings.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Interact with other students and arrange more private and intimate events.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: In Toronto it was pretty easy since it is diverse city, but the academic structure was weird to begin with.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to events, look at the Canadian memes and see sports or local news.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Food types

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People were open and easygoing. You could talk about everything.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Have all the money you need and a bit extra for fun
2. Remember to take initiative
3. Keep up from the beginning

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There is a website for building your schedule and avoiding course conflict, use it wisely :)
https://registrar.yorku.ca/enrol/guide/vsb

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The academics and adding on to my academic profile. Meeting nice people was definitely also awesome.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting there and the process beforehand (covid19)

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Expect higher expectations of your own participation in academics

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
